method: git diff --name-status per candidate against baseline, then pairwise set intersection of changed paths, then per-file hunk-level semantic review of every intersecting file. No cherry-pick-and-accept-default-resolution.

overlaps.candidate_a_change: NEW-301: consume canonical LiDAR runtime spec (resolve_active_lidars) and set LiDAR blueprint attributes from the spec instead of hard-coded per-call defaults.
overlaps.candidate_b_change: NEW-333: governed camera photometric response profile. Adds camera_response_profile to __init__ (env UP_CAMERA_RESPONSE_PROFILE or strict baseline default), applies apply_response_profile per camera and records per-camera reports.
overlaps.reasoning: Different modality and different call sites. A edits the LiDAR loop (lidar_items), B edits the camera loop plus the constructor signature. Touching the same file is not the same authority.
overlaps.resolution: Auto-merged; both contracts preserved and verified present in the merged file: canonical_lidar_spec import + resolve_active_lidars call in the LiDAR loop, and camera_response_profile/apply_response_profile in the camera path.
overlaps.post_merge_defect_fixed: A's _select_capture_profile_items still passed every calibration LiDAR entry into the spawn loop, so an inactive entry (middle_lidar_old) hit A's own NEW-301 'not in canonical active spec' RuntimeError and aborted the entire rig. This is an A-intra semantic bug that a text-level merge cannot surface. Fixed: spawn only the canonical active set; a missing active LiDAR is a fail-closed RuntimeError.

overlaps.candidate_a_change: NEW-300/301: restrict the spawn loop to the canonical active LiDAR set.
overlaps.candidate_b_change: NEW-333: add camera_response_profile param and apply profile_attributes to the camera attribute dict via setdefault, keeping geometry owned by the method.
overlaps.reasoning: A's hunk is in the LiDAR spawn path; B's is in the camera attribute builder (_camera_attributes) plus __init__. Independent contracts.
overlaps.resolution: Auto-merged; both preserved (canonical_lidar_spec import + active_lidars loop; camera_response_profile + profile_attributes setdefault).

overlaps.candidate_a_change: NEW-299/301: consume canonical LiDAR spec for attribute setting and return runtime rig identity.
overlaps.resolution: Taken from A unchanged, then repaired: resolve_active_lidars(data, ...) referenced an undefined name (load_calib returns cams, lids, not data), so the canonical path would raise NameError at runtime; and a missing active LiDAR produced a warning rather than a failure. Both fixed in the integration commit.

overlaps.candidate_b_change: NEW-326/327/328: route initialize() through TrafficManagerSession; seed from the governed seed tree; fail closed on unresolved seed.
overlaps.resolution: Preserved as a compatibility facade over traffic_manager_session.py. It does not implement its own TM authority; it constructs one session and delegates. No second TM wrapper was created.

overlaps.candidate_b_change: NEW-316/317/318/327: governed weather resolver, per-arm weather binding, complete weather schema, seed tree.
overlaps.resolution: Preserved. Weather authority remains weather_spec.py + deterministic_weather.py.

overlaps.candidate_a_change: NEW-294: schema v1 requires crs and geo_reference, digest and sequence validation.
overlaps.candidate_b_change: no change to route_manifest.py (B touches rq3_capture_contract.py instead)
overlaps.resolution: Preserved as authoritative. This strengthening exposed a stale production test helper (see INTEGRATION_DECISIONS.json), which was repaired to supply the now-required frame fields plus a new test asserting the frame requirement.

Preserved as authoritative, then repaired. Frame identity was compared as raw strings (declared 'EPSG:25832' vs map '+proj=utm +zone=32 ...'), so a genuinely shared frame was always reported as unshared; and a manifest whose declared CRS contradicted its own geo_reference was accepted. Both repaired fail-closed.

duplicate_authority_audit.method: search the merged tree for a second implementation of each governed concern
duplicate_authority_audit.second_lidar_spec: none - ultimate_pipeline/sensors/canonical_lidar_spec.py is the only LiDAR runtime-spec resolver; all three rig constructors (ThesisSensorRig, DominikSensorSetup, attach_sensors_safe) import it
duplicate_authority_audit.second_weather_spec: none - weather_spec.py (resolve/identity/apply/verify) + deterministic_weather.py (frame-driven schedule) are the only weather authorities
duplicate_authority_audit.second_tm_wrapper: none - traffic_manager_session.TrafficManagerSession is the single TM authority; fixed_traffic_manager.py delegates to it
duplicate_authority_audit.second_seed_tree: none - seed_tree.py is the only RNG/seed-tree authority; deterministic_weather uses its own seeded random.Random instance and does not touch the process-global RNG
duplicate_authority_audit.second_calibration_authority: none - calibration_authority.py delegates to sensors/calibration_contract.py as the canonical validator; heuristic exports are explicitly non-authoritative
duplicate_authority_audit.second_route_execution_engine: none - route_execution.py is the only strict route executor; legacy apply_transform movement is not an alternative authority
duplicate_authority_audit.competing_rig_transforms: found and removed - ultimate_pipeline/sensors/rig_transforms.py self-imported and read calib_data.json from cwd at import time, making the sensors package non-import-safe. It was relocated to ultimate_pipeline/tools/rig_transforms_check.py, rewritten to delegate to transform_conventions (the real pose authority) with no module-level execution. Production callers: zero (only self-reference plus one historical report mention).

semantic_conflicts_found.detail: Candidate A's NEW-295 module decided frame sharing by string equality between an EPSG authority code and a PROJ.4 string, which is never equal. This is a false-negative machine for frame binding: it would reject correct paired captures and, combined with the missing manifest self-consistency check, accept a route declaring one CRS while carrying another zone's parameters.
semantic_conflicts_found.resolution: Repaired in the integration commit with canonical_crs_identity() (lazy pyproj) and fail-closed comparison. Unknown/unresolvable CRS is never treated as a match.

semantic_conflicts_found.concern: inactive LiDAR entries vs rig construction
semantic_conflicts_found.detail: A's own two NEW-300/NEW-301 changes conflict: the canonical active-set restriction in _select_capture_profile_items was not applied, so an inactive calibration entry would abort the whole rig via A's own RuntimeError.
semantic_conflicts_found.resolution: Repaired: spawn set = canonical active LiDARs only; missing active LiDAR = fail-closed.

semantic_conflicts_found.concern: NEW-299 rig identity was not hashable/reachable
semantic_conflicts_found.detail: A imported canonical_lidar_hash into thesis_sensor_rig.py but never used it; no runtime rig identity was produced, so NEW-299's 'hash the actually spawned rig' contract was unmet.
semantic_conflicts_found.resolution: Added ThesisSensorRig.runtime_rig_identity() over the spawned sensors' effective attributes, recorded at the end of spawn_rig, including the canonical LiDAR spec hash so inactive entries cannot affect identity.

compatible_independent_changes_confirmed: A route authority + B environment authority do not compete for any function
B camera response (photometric) vs A canonical LiDAR spec (geometric/attribute) are disjoint concerns
B seed tree feeds B TM and B weather without competing with A route framing
